Interface: Explicit finite-dimensional rational local generators and product start, finite explicit targets; one extension adds finitely many global gate states with a compatibility condition and optional synchronized product-stationary reset. A separate stationary sampler permits arbitrary unbalanced finite gate generators.
Failure: The source reports internal proofs and small floating checks, not an implemented general certified solver. These are distinct interfaces; they do not combine into one unrestricted interacting-chain theorem. The stationary sampler assumes fair bits and expected polynomial work, not a worst-case time bound; its fixture uses a small exact-state oracle, not the scalable acquired oracle.

The packet contains separate internal candidates built around finite-rank boundary resolvents. The unbalanced-gate stationary-observable theorem used by the exact-sampling corollary is a distinct interface and has its own source record. First, for independent irreducible finite-state local CTMCs with explicit rational generators, a product start and a finite explicit target list, it gives an additive CDF approximation with polynomial bit complexity in the explicit input and log(1/epsilon), without enumerating the product state space. The proof uses a sector bound for nonreversible local generators.

A further model permits recurring transitions on a finite list of global gate configurations and synchronized resets, subject to an explicit compatibility condition preserving the product stationary law. These interactions recur and may change multiple coordinates. Separately, a corollary claims exact stationary samples with expected polynomial bit cost for an arbitrary unbalanced finite gate generator under an ideal fair-bit interface.

The general nonreversible quadrature theorem is not implemented as a certified solver. The exact-sampler fixture uses a small exact-state oracle and does not demonstrate the scalable acquired-prefix oracle. No worst-case termination bound, generic succinct interactions, independent correctness certification or novelty conclusion follows. The statements have distinct assumptions and are not one general interacting-chain theorem.

synchronized stationary resets handled by a further small Woodbury solve.

1. Interface and result

Input: n independent irreducible continuous-time chains, with explicitly given
d_i by d_i rational row-generators Q_i, rational product initial law
mu=otimes_i mu_i, a deduplicated list B of m distinct product configurations,
a nonnegative rational time t, and rational epsilon in (0,1/2). Write
d=max_i d_i, N=prod_i d_i, Q=sum_i Q_i (tensor-coordinate sum),
tau_B=inf{t>=0:X_t in B}. Degenerate one-state coordinates may be removed.

entire binary input length, m, and log(1/epsilon), and does not enumerate N

dimension d, but d itself is bounded by input length. Its operations are
small local matrix exponentials, products of their selected entries, scalar

factor polynomial in the possibly exponential inverse product spectral gap,
inverse stationary mass of B, or inverse hitting rate: only their bit lengths
enter. This is an additive CDF query, not exact symbolic output or an unbiased
single-sample simulator.

PERSISTENT COUPLING EXTENSION: FINITE GLOBAL GATES AND SYNCHRONIZED RESETS
Internal theorem candidate, 2026-10-10. Algebraic composition, no novelty claim.

The base theorem in RESULT.txt computes an additive-epsilon CDF of the first
hit of m explicit product configurations by independent rational finite CTMCs.
This extension permits genuine, indefinitely recurring interactions while
retaining polynomial bit complexity in the succinct input and log(1/epsilon).

Operational input class

Let Q0 be the tensor-coordinate sum of explicitly supplied irreducible local
generators Q_i, with product stationary law pi0 and product initial law mu.
Give k distinct global configurations G={g_1,...,g_k} and an explicitly
supplied rational k by k row-generator Gamma. Check exactly that

    sum_{j=1}^k pi0(g_j) Gamma_{j,l}=0  for every l.        (1)

Thus the restriction of pi0 to G is a strictly positive, not necessarily
normalized stationary measure for Gamma. Optionally supply a nonnegative
rational global reset rate r. The complete generator on the N=prod_i d_i
product states is

    Q=Q0+E_G Gamma E_G^T+r(1 pi0^T-I).                  (2)

Here E_G selects the listed configurations. The gate term triggers a jump
between global configurations when the chain visits one, possibly changing
every coordinate at once. Gamma can be nonreversible; directed cycles of
three or more gates are allowed. The reset term, when present, independently
resamples *all* coordinates at one common Poisson event time from pi0. These
events recur indefinitely; (2) does not merely modify an absorbing target.
Both terms are valid generators and preserve pi0. Q remains irreducible.

For an explicit target set B of m configurations, rational t>=0, and rational
epsilon>0, Pr_mu(tau_B<=t) can be computed to additive epsilon in bit time
polynomial in the entire input length, k, m, and log(1/epsilon), without
enumerating N. The reset rate may be zero; the gate list may be empty.

EXACT INDEPENDENT STATIONARY SAMPLES FROM UNBALANCED GLOBAL-GATE CHAINS
Internal constructive corollary, 2026-10-10. No priority claim.

Input class: the rational product-chain plus arbitrary recurring k-gate
generator Q=Q0+E_G Gamma E_G^T of UNBALANCED_STEADY_STATE.txt. Every local
Q_i is irreducible; Gamma needs no balance condition. The product state
space has N=prod_i d_i configurations, potentially exponential in input.

Theorem. A randomized algorithm outputs a configuration with distribution
EXACTLY equal to the unique stationary law pi of Q. It uses fair random
bits and has expected bit complexity polynomial in the full explicit input
length, n, k, and local dimensions. It neither enumerates N nor receives
pi or a mixing-time oracle. Independent repetitions give independent exact
stationary samples. Almost-sure termination and finite expected cost are
guaranteed; no worst-case finite running-time bound is asserted.

argument works with ANY destination y, not just one fixed x*: from every
x to every y there is a coordinate path of length at most L, padded by
self-loops to exactly L uniformization ticks. Thus

    [exp(TQ)](x,y)>=eta=(p/4)^L>0   for every x,y.   (1)

Stationarity gives pi(y)=sum_x pi(x)[exp(TQ)](x,y)>=eta. Every nonempty
prefix cylinder C_h={x:x_1=h_1,...,x_j=h_j} contains a full state and
therefore pi(C_h)>=eta. eta is rational and log(1/eta) is polynomial in
input length. This lower bound is deliberately conservative; it is never
paid as a numeric inverse in the sampler's running time.

Proof 2: polynomial-precision prefix mass oracle

are included in this certified absolute bound. No exact expanded rational
